title: Offsets fitted to 3 to 20 target donors increased expected test error in two selected Allen transfer models
abstract: We tested whether a small target-donor calibration set improves transfer of 50 Hz synaptic response predictions between selected Allen mouse visual-cortex and human temporal-cortex connections. The sample has 493 mouse and 162 human excitatory connections. An offset fitted to five donors increased empirical test error by about 16% in both directions across 200 donor splits. The offset still beat ridge models fitted only to those target donors. A post hoc exact finite-population identity separates bias removal from calibration variance. For these fixed source models and observed donor populations, offsets fitted to 3 to 20 donors increase expected test error. The exact five-donor increases are 13.69% and 13.76%. Species and region are confounded. Shared response estimates, selected records and inferred donor groups limit biological use. Conditional bootstrap intervals do not include full source and calibration-fit uncertainty. Original code, proof, figure, aggregate evidence and external retrieval steps are supplied. External records are not bundled.

display.caption: Target test error by calibration budget in two selected Allen slice transfer models. The source-only rule has lower error than an offset fitted on 3 to 20 target donors.

citations.reason: Tests its stated open question about small target calibration sets, using new simpler models and original code on overlapping data.
